articles.content: Olivia Colman’s steamy romance, where she plays a woman in love with a wicker man, becomes an unlikely pick for the theme park-like cinema experience What does Olivia Colman’s hot sex with a basket tell us about heteropessimism? ‘I saw the script and went: oooh!’ Olivia Colman and Alexander Skårsgard on their steamy folk-horror movie Wicker Since its introduction in the US in 2014, 4DX, the rollercoaster-ization of the theatrical experience, has primarily been the purview of action movies. And for good reason; the high-speed chases of a Fast and Furious movie, or repetitive battle sequences of an Avatar saga, translate easily to the moving chairs, scent machines and wind/water sprayers of the format, which more closely resembles an amusement park ride than cinema. As a longtime fan of plane turbulence-style seat movement, I thought the immersive pleasures of 4DX – the second most-popular of so-called large premium formats in the US, behind Imax – reached its zenith in the summer of 2024 with the release of Twisters, a perfectly fine action movie about tornadoes that became an 11/10 experience when jostled in one’s seat to actual wind and rain. But a recent, unexpected candidate is finally pushing the bounds of 4DX again, making the most of the format’s potential to enhance the sensorial joys of cinema. Continue reading...

articles.title: If hackers can take control of a supermarket freezer, how vulnerable is other tech?
articles.summary: Dozens of shops across European countries have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their fridges.
articles.content: Dozens of shops across European countries have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their fridges.
articles.aiArticle:
A widespread digital intrusion has disabled refrigeration units in dozens of commercial storefronts throughout multiple European nations, according to a report by BBC News. The security breach targeted the temperature control systems of supermarket cooling equipment, resulting in widespread food spoilage across the affected retail locations. 

While the exact mechanics of the breach remain under investigation, the incident highlights a growing vulnerability in the interconnected hardware used by modern retail chains. Smart appliances and commercial Internet of Things devices have increasingly become targets for malicious actors seeking to disrupt daily operations. 

## ## The Expanding Threat to Commercial Infrastructure

According to the BBC News report, the malicious campaign successfully compromised store equipment across international borders, leaving business owners to deal with significant inventory losses. The deliberate manipulation of commercial refrigeration units demonstrates how physical retail infrastructure can be disabled remotely when connected to standard networks. 

This disruption follows [a fresh wave of cyberattacks that has hit Europe’s supermarket refrigerators, destroying food across countries](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/a-fresh-wave-of-cyberattacks-has-hit-europe-s-supermarket-refrigerators-destroying), indicating that retail supply chains face persistent and coordinated digital threats. Security analysts note that many commercial facilities rely on legacy software or default administrative passwords, making them easy targets for automated malware or targeted intrusion attempts. 

## ## Why This Matters

As modern retail operations become heavily reliant on automated climate control and inventory tracking, the stakes for physical security have shifted toward digital defenses. When remote attackers can manipulate basic hardware like supermarket refrigerators, the financial toll on small and large businesses alike can be immediate and severe. Beyond the direct cost of spoiled goods, these incidents expose how vulnerabilities in commercial IoT devices can compromise public trust in food supply logistics and essential retail services. 

Industry observers also point to parallels in other sectors, such as the digital risks surrounding critical national infrastructure like the [control of Britain’s 39m smart meters passed to a non-profit startup](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/control-of-britain-s-m-smart-meters-passes-to-non-profit-startup), which highlight the massive scale of connected devices potentially open to interference. As more physical machinery gets wired into centralized management networks, the potential surface area for disruptive attacks grows exponentially. 

## ## What to Watch

Security researchers will be closely monitoring whether the perpetrators behind the European grocery store attacks issue ransom demands or if the incident was purely designed to cause operational chaos. Investigators are expected to release further technical details regarding the specific vulnerabilities exploited in the cooling systems, which could prompt regulatory bodies to impose stricter cybersecurity standards on commercial appliance manufacturers. 

Sources: [BBC News](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckpqg8lve73go?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

While consumers and energy providers have long grappled with the complexities of digital meter integration, the arrival of a non-profit startup aims to chart a different course for the network's backend operations.

Smart meters are increasingly central to modern domestic energy grids, allowing households to monitor consumption in real time and helping utility providers balance supply and demand. ## The Grid Protectors Program in Georgia

According to a report by **The Verge**, the artificial intelligence developer announced on **Monday** that it will launch its **Grid Protectors Program** at a planned data center in **Effingham County, Georgia**. The company states that the facility will pledge to free up as much as **1,000 megawatts** of electricity when the regional grid faces extreme conditions or sudden shortages. According to the publication, this capacity is designed to support the surrounding community during crises, attempting to counter growing skepticism over the hefty resource demands of modern AI infrastructure.

As large-scale computing facilities expand rapidly across various regions, local communities have increasingly pushed back against the massive strain these installations place on public utilities and municipal resources. ## Why This Matters

As context, the rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence models requires unprecedented levels of computational power, driving tech giants to build massive server farms that consume electricity on the scale of small cities. This surge in power demand has sparked intense friction with local residents and environmental advocates who worry about grid stability and rising utility bills. Initiatives like the Grid Protectors Program represent an effort by developers to ease public opposition and secure necessary regulatory approvals by framing massive computing hubs as emergency assets rather than purely parasitic power drains.

articles.summary: Marvell's planned purchase of Lumentum is one of the biggest acquisitions in tech history. And they both have the same strategic investor: Nvidia.
articles.content: Marvell's planned purchase of Lumentum is one of the biggest acquisitions in tech history. And they both have the same strategic investor: Nvidia.
articles.aiArticle:
One of the largest corporate acquisitions in the history of the technology sector is currently underway, with **Marvell** moving to purchase **Lumentum** for a staggering **$115 billion**, according to a report by **TechCrunch**. 

## Shared Backing and Strategic Alignment

The multi-billion-dollar transaction brings together two major industry players that share a common thread in their corporate backing. As noted by TechCrunch, both firms count **Nvidia** as a strategic investor. This shared financial backing points toward deeper consolidation within the semiconductor and optical networking supply chains, which have faced intense pressure and shifting demands as corporations race to build out infrastructure for modern computing workloads. 

## Market Context and Structural Pressures

Corporate tie-ups of this magnitude often reflect broader macroeconomic anxieties and intense competitive positioning across the global technology sector. While major enterprises continue pouring billions into advanced data centers, broader industry trends show that technology leaders are constantly seeking efficiencies, as highlighted in broader discussions on [how enterprise AI tools impact executive leadership and organizational workflows](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/ai-can-make-tech-ceos-lives-easier-what-about-everyone-else). 

> **Context:** Mega-mergers in the hardware and semiconductor space fundamentally alter pricing power and supply dynamics for downstream buyers, particularly as hyperscale cloud providers demand specialized components to accelerate specialized computing tasks. 

## Regulatory Scrutiny and Future Outlook

Transactions crossing the hundred-billion-dollar threshold invariably invite rigorous antitrust investigations from regulatory bodies in the United States and internationally. Antitrust lawyers and market analysts will likely scrutinize whether the overlapping investor base or the combined market share of Marvell and Lumentum harms competitive access for rival hardware makers. 

> **What to watch:** Observers should monitor upcoming regulatory filings for potential antitrust probes, shareholder voting timelines, and statements from major customers regarding supply chain continuity.

articles.title: Why Peacock is making a huge bet on YouTube
articles.summary: Today, I’m talking with Matt Strauss, who is now chairman of the NBCUniversal Media Group. This is Matt’s second time joining me on the show, and there’s been a whole lot of organizational and structural change at NBCU since the last time he and I spoke just…
articles.content: Today, I’m talking with Matt Strauss, who is now chairman of the NBCUniversal Media Group. This is Matt’s second time joining me on the show, and there’s been a whole lot of organizational and structural change at NBCU since the last time he and I spoke just two years ago — pure Decoder bait. First, about a month after Matt was on the show, Comcast spun off most of the NBCU cable channels into something called Versant. That’s when Matt’s title changed from heading up just the direct-to-consumer offering — meaning Peacock, plus some other streaming services — to heading up the whole thing, across all distribution. And now, Comcast is spinning off the NBCU business entirely into a whole new standalone company. Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . That’s a lot to have going on all at once! And meanwhile, it’s only just this year that Peacock became an actual profitable business at all — and it’s still pretty far away from being anything like the juggernaut that Netflix is. But what NBCU has, and what Peacock has, that the rest of the streaming industry is still trying to wrap its head around, is live sports. Sports are huge. They held up the cable industry for years, they held up broadcast, and now they’re the big thing that could make streaming a winner for NBC. One thing before we start: You’ll hear me ask Matt about the red company and the blue company. That’s just my way of getting Matt to talk about Netflix and Skydance, the company that now owns both Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery. I think he did a good job playing along. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube, where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday. Okay: Matt Strauss, chairman of the NBCU Media Group. Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Matt Strauss, you are the chairman of the NBCUniversal Media Group. Welcome back to Decoder . Thank you so much, Nilay. It’s great to be back. I am very excited to talk to you. There’s a lot going on in the media. It is a tumultuous time in Hollywood. I have to tell the audience that you and I are speaking minutes after Anthropic filed its S-1 , and all of humanity is going to be turned into AI. Who knows what entertainment we’ll be watching in the future? There’s a lot going on. Let’s start at the very beginning of this. You have a new job since last time you were on the show. Last time, you were the head of Direct-to-Consumer — you were basically the head of Peacock and the other apps inside the family. Now you’re the chairman of NBCUniversal Media Group. What’s the new job? What does that mean? NBCUniversal Media Group is comprised of certain services within NBC. It’s the broadcast network, it’s Bravo, it’s Peacock, it’s NBC Sports. We also have NBC News and Telemundo. One of the things that we recognized, especially when we spun off some of our cable assets last year into Versant, was that the assets we had truly worked better together. NBC has been like a megaphone. Given the reach of NBC, it’s been incredibly strategic in growing Peacock, which is a bit ironic because I think so many people believed that broadcasting was a bit of a relic of the past in this digital world, but it’s actually proven to be the opposite. As things have gotten more fragmented, having a broadcast network is actually a superpower because we’re continuing to see ratings growth. That has been really helpful as we’ve been building out Peacock. But actually, Peacock was also finding new audiences, like cord cutters or people who maybe didn’t grow up watching NBC or some of our cable networks. So, Peacock’s also been really strategic in reaching and driving people back to NBC and Bravo. So, I think that flywheel is where we recognized that we needed to start operating differently. I’ve been a huge advocate of what I like to call “centers of excellence” in how I like to structure the business, which is, content first and platform second. How do we get maximum reach, maximum engagement? That really required us thinking differently about how we were running the business. Essentially, instead of having a programming group within broadcast and a programming group within streaming, we just collapsed the business. Now you’ve got one programming team, one marketing team, one product and technology team, one decision sciences and research team, and one advertising team. They’re all incentivized around continuing to grow the portfolio, get that maximum reach, maximum engagement, and drive top-line revenue. I think that structure, which we put in place about 18 months ago, is contributing to a lot of the success that we’re seeing now. Even if you look at 2026, NBC is the number one network in total viewers. We had an unbelievable early part of the year with “Legendary February,” which you might remember. That’s when we had the Super Bowl, the Milan Cortina Olympics, and the NBA All-Star Game. In 17 days, we reached over 225 million viewers. This summer, we had Love Island , which was the number one show of the summer for streaming. You had the World Cup, which was the number one Spanish-language sporting event in US history on Telemundo and Peacock. We had a show called The Five-Star Weekend , which was our number one scripted drama. Now, we’ve led ourselves into the fall, where we have Sunday Night Football, which has been the number one show for 15 consecutive years. We had a great kickoff with over 25 million viewers. We just had the NBA tip-off last week with the Knicks and the Sixers, which is the number one rated tip-off in NBA history. So, it does feel like we’re firing on all cylinders in how we’re trying to operate with this, again, content-first-platform-second mantra. But just to go one level deeper, a big part of this strategy is figuring out how do we move audiences across platforms. For example, when I mentioned that Love Island was the number one streaming show of the summer, 40 percent of those Love Island viewers also tuned in to watch the World Cup. So, migrating viewers back and forth across the portfolio is a critical part of how we see ourselves continuing to grow. But to effectuate that, you need to structure yourself in a way where people are incentivized along that vision. We’re still evolving as an organization, but I’m really proud of some of the milestones and accomplishments that we’ve made as a team. I love my job. I feel like I’ve got the best job in the industry at the moment. It is a tumultuous time in Hollywood, and you seem like one of the happiest people in the industry right at the second. That is very notable. You’re a Decoder pro, you brought up structure. I’m dying to ask you about the Decision Sciences Group. That’s the other question I ask everybody. But let me just back out for one second. You’re describing quite a lot of freedom in rethinking how something like NBCUniversal would work. You mentioned the Versant spin, so CNBC, MS Now, and a bunch of channels went that way. I’m on its networks all the time. I would describe the folks at Versant as feeling more free. They’re disconnected from the battleship that was Comcast and NBCUniversal. They can go try whatever they want to try. They’re energized by it in some ways. Then, Comcast looked at NBCUniversal and said, “We’re going to spin off that off as well. We’re going to be the cable business and NBCUniversal will be the entertainment business, and now you’re in charge of that.” You’re like a 20-year Comcast veteran. I think you got your start doing cable boxes. Yep. I started in 2004 at Comcast. Just tell me about that process. We spun off CNBC and MS Now into Versant. Now we’re looking at this company. We ought to spin off NBCUniversal as well. Just tell me about how that came about. What was that moment like? Did you all sit in a boardroom? Did it come down from on high? How did that happen? Well, that decision really was made by Brian Roberts and Mike Cavanagh. Candidly, I was not in the room when that decision was made, but I think if you were to ask people at NBCUniversal, it makes strategic sense. Do you feel that same sense of freedom? You know what? I think that there’s an energy. When people show up here, they feel very passionate about what they do. They believe in our strategy, they believe in our portfolio. Look at NBCUniversal more broadly. Before, I was describing the Media Group, but that is one piece of the broader company. You have Universal Pictures and Universal Television, which have obviously been having an unbelievable summer with The Odyssey and Obsession . You’ve got Universal’s theme parks and experiences. We opened up Epic Universe last year. We opened up a kids theme park in Texas. We announced we’re going to open up a theme park in the UK . We have Sky, which was part of the company but more squarely sat within Comcast Cable. Now that’s going to migrate over to the new NBCUniversal as part of this restructure. Then, you have these media assets, which I spoke about earlier. So, you’ve got this unbelievable portfolio. I think that people here really believe in our growth and that if we’re a separate company, it’s going to allow us to move faster. It’s going to let us have more clarity around where we want to make capital allocations and decisions. There are a few areas that really play to our strengths as an organization. One of them is live sports and live events. That’s always been a part of NBCUniversal that we’re really known for. If you just look at the sports portfolio that we have, Nilay, we’ve got NFL, NBA, MLB, the Big Ten Conference, the Premier League. We’ve got the Olympics with the IOC. You’ve got this unbelievable portfolio of sports content, and that’s a strategic asset when we’re partnering with the leagues because we believe in broadcast. We believe in broad reach. We’re not trying to put everything exclusively on a streaming platform. In 2026, we’ve demonstrated across almost every single sport that we can actually continue to grow ratings and reach new audiences, which is something that’s becoming more and more complicated. Can I ask about that? Because you also run Peacock, which is a paid streamer where you can access sports. When you say grow ratings on broadcast, are more people putting up antennas to watch sports over the air? No. What I mean… By the way, about 20 percent of TV households in this country do still use over-the-air antennas as— Oh, we have lots of listeners who are going to tell you that’s the best picture quality you can get. Yeah. It is amazing picture quality, especially if you live in the right look angle where you could pick up the signal. It comes back to what I said earlier about managing as a portfolio. We don’t think of it as a broadcast business sitting next to a streaming business. We really position ourselves as a digital-first company trying to get that maximum reach. When we look at the ratings, we’re combining what you would think of as more traditional ratings for linear television with streaming and all of our digital platforms. Whether that’s DVR or TV Everywhere, we aggregate it into one platform. When you look at it through that lens, which is just audience, we’ve actually demonstrated that across almost every sport — NFL, NBA, or MLB — the total viewers that we are reaching now are, in some cases, the highest they’ve been in decades. Even the Super Bowl, which we had earlier this year on NBC, reached about 137 million viewers at its peak, and that’s across all of our platforms. That Super Bowl was the highest-rated live event in NBC’s 100-year anniversary, which is this year. It’s kind of counterintuitive, but what we’re showing is that when we start operating as one, we can reach new audiences and we can aggregate them. We are demonstrating that not just across sports. There’s even something like the Thanksgiving Day Parade, which has been an institution on NBC for 99 years. This past Thanksgiving Day Parade was the highest-rated parade we have had in the company’s history. So, there’s a renaissance happening around live. In a world of instant gratification, on demand, and watching what you want when you want, the fact that you’re now seeing more and more viewers wanting the collective consciousness of social viewing, things that still matter in today’s society, that actually plays to our strengths. And we’re seeing that manifest itself with higher ratings. But as I mentioned, it’s also a big part of our strategy. It was a big part of our Peacock strategy, which was a bit of an anomaly when we launched Peacock six years ago. It’s also a huge part of what I think NBC does well, which is that we create these big tentpole events and we’re able to shine a light on them and get huge audiences that are continuing to show up, even in a world of fragmentation and cord-cutting. It’s interesting that you’ve described it as content first and platform second, and then you’re describing your approach to ratings as agnostic to distribution. You’re just sort of combining everything and saying, “This is the number of people we reached.” Well, take something like the Milan Cortina Olympics. This is an interesting example. What you’re really looking for is incrementality. Is this going to drive incremental subscribers, and can I get the right wholesale economics where this is also incremental on the revenue side? What’s interesting about YouTube is that I think it’s a win-win. It’s a win-win because there’s multiple components to this deal. One aspect is that there’s going to be a bundle launched next year with the ad-supported tier of Peacock and a tier of YouTube Premium. Now, you’re going to get access to all of the benefits of YouTube Premium with the ad-supported version of Peacock. We believe that these are mostly incremental subscribers, or people who do not necessarily have Peacock today. So, it’s going to grow Peacock while adding more value to YouTube Premium. My prediction is that if you and I have a conversation a year from now, Peacock will be one of the top distributed streaming services in the United States. Do you care that you don’t own your last-mile customer that way? This was a big reason everyone went to streaming. They were selling their content to Netflix, and they realized Netflix owned the customer. Now we’ve all got to stand up our own streaming services because we want to own the customer and the cable bundle is falling apart. Do you care now that as you rebundle, YouTube will own the customer in some important way? I think that when you say “own the customer,” really what you’re talking about is, “How do I get the ability to personalize the experience so that I could super-serve an individual both with content and with advertising? What’s ultimately going to create the monetization engine that we need?” I was describing the value of Peacock and the fact that 80 percent of our subs are on the ad platform and that we typically charge premium CPMs (cost per mille) because we have this ability to super-serve our fandoms and franchises, and we have the data to do it. I think that the relationship with YouTube that we announced this summer is going to allow us to have a much deeper integration with YouTube on the data side as well as the integration with FreeWheel. So, we’re at a point where we’re almost indifferent again about where somebody consumes the content— FreeWheel is your programmatic advertising business. Yes. That was a critical part to this unlock with YouTube because we can create a bundle that is going to drive incremental subscribers and value. To your point, YouTube TV is the fastest-growing pay TV distributor. I think the pay TV ecosystem has been declining at a 6-7 percent CAGR. Over the past five years, YouTube TV has grown at a 26-27 percent CAGR. It has over 10 million subscribers and are likely going to be the number one pay TV distributor in the next couple of years. We extended our linear portfolio agreement with YouTube TV, which is going to provide us stability and growth on that part of our portfolio as well. What we were just describing around having a much deeper integration with the data, analytics, and targeting is going to allow us to monetize our inventory. It’s all of these pieces. We think this is an example of how we’re trying to think differently, or how we’re trying to be innovative and identify strategic partners. I don’t know if the red company or the blue company would be in a position to do the kind of deal that I’m describing, but it’s precisely because we are independent and looking to be more flexible. I think that actually becomes a calling card for how we could work with other companies in a way that is really transformative. Let me ask you, I think the red company hypothetically got turned upside down because it relied on data too much for the programming and now it’s going to change a bunch of programming executives, so we’ll see where it goes. The hypothetical blue company led by the hypothetical son of a billionaire is out in the market. It made a big content acquisition. He’s saying, “Oh, we’re going to invest in technology and we’ll compete with Northern California. We’ll compete with any of the platforms based on our technology bet.” To me, that seems like an old story where I know the ending . Trying to run at TikTok’s technology without the content is just going to get you backwards. If you were running the blue company, how would you think about technology in that way? Well, I’m going to answer the question based on how I’m running our company. The blue company’s new. Anything could happen with the blue company. I think my answer, though, would not change depending on where I sat within this industry. I believe that we need to be an open ecosystem, that you’ve got to go where the viewers are. That’s what led us to make a lot of strategic decisions, whether it’s the deal that I just described with YouTube, or the channel deals for the ad-free tier of Peacock with Amazon and Roku. We’ve done bundling deals. We’ve done a bundle deal with Apple. We’ve done a bundle deal with Walmart. You’re trying to give consumers choices. Everything I’ve done in my career has always been around the north star of giving consumers choice: what they want, when they want, where they want. That, to me, has been the mantra for how we’re trying to build our company. All of that being said, I am still also a huge believer in the product, the technology, and the experience. You may be able to watch the Olympics on another platform through NBC or Peacock, but I truly believe the best experience was on Peacock. Are you allowed to say that on other people’s networks? Can you go on to Amazon channels and say, “This is great, but if you want the first class, get out of this app and open Peacock?” Do they let you say that? Well, I wouldn’t say it that way, though. First of all, I think when somebody subscribes to Peacock, they should be able to access our service regardless of the platform. In that respect, we do cross-authentication — meaning you can subscribe and watch on Peacock, or you could subscribe and access our service through channels. I’m not here to tell the consumer what the best experience is. I think that we lead by example. The consumers vote based on where they ultimately decide to engage. If you want to get access to some of these cool features that I’m describing, if you want to play a game that we created, or if you want to listen to a podcast, or… I’ll give you another example. We’re testing our membership program because we shouldn’t think of viewers as subscribers, we should think of them as members. What are the other values that you can get as part of being a member? Well, maybe some of those values could be based on your tenure or your level of engagement. Maybe you get discounts to NBC merchandise. Maybe you get special access when you go to Universal theme parks. Maybe you get discounts from some of our advertising partners, like Domino’s. How do we start to add more value? But maybe that membership is only available when you’re on our platform. I think of it more as needing to give consumers the choice. At the same time, we are investing in product and technology and on experiences that are really meant to be delivered upon the platform that we have created. We’ve got an unbelievable team, in my opinion, that has created a best-in-class, scalable platform that not only powers Peacock, but also powers Sky’s Now TV. It’s the same platform that we’ve also distributed to dozens of countries around the world. We’ve got a world-class team that is really trying to transform, surprise, and delight viewers in a way that I’m not sure other platforms are going to be able to do around our content and franchises, especially when it comes to especially these major tentpole events. I want to end by asking maybe the most important question of all. We’re talking a lot about internet-distributed businesses and consumers signing up for services and being able to churn and quit. There are a lot of free market dynamics there, which I think are very powerful and very important. That means you get to program whatever you want to program. You have chosen live in sports and, importantly, you mentioned news at the top of this conversation. NBC News is part of this portfolio. NBC News is also distributed over broadcast. It’s distributed over the air. The Trump administration and FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, in particular, has expressed a lot of desire to pressure broadcast networks because you use the public spectrum, particularly news networks. He’s withheld the broadcast licenses for ABC stations, for example. He has threatened the other broadcast networks. There’s a lot of pressure on NBC News. How are you handling that? Are you pushing back? Because that is the one place where you’re not allowed to just do whatever you want, right? The government gets to tell you what to say in an increasingly uncomfortable way. Yeah. Look, I think I give a lot of credit to [NBCUniversal News Group Chairman] Cesar Conde and the NBC News organization who are big believers in freedom of speech and freedom of the press. I think they’re doing a fantastic job. When it comes to distribution of our content, especially our news programming, I think that’s an example where it’s available everywhere. I mean, we truly make it available not only on Peacock, NBC, and over the air, but through Fast TV, NBC News Now— Have you made this argument to the administration? Because I’ve met a lot of FCC chairmen over the years, and until Carr showed up, the argument they would make is that we have to get away from overthinking broadcast because the audience is everywhere, and they don’t actually make a distinction between broadcast television and cable. That was a Republican talking point for years and years. This is nonsense. The other version is that everyone’s on TikTok and the industry has to contend with that in some way. We should get more people internet access because that will actually even the playing field. Now we’ve come to, “You have to use the spectrum in the public interest.” It is different and the government should impose some speech pressure — which again, I think is inappropriate — but that is a new argument. I’m wondering if you have said to the administration, “Look, the consumer doesn’t make this distinction and we as a company aren’t making this distinction.” Well, I’ve not had those direct conversations myself. Obviously, we have a government affairs team that works very closely with regulators in DC. There’s probably no better time to be alive than right now when it comes to being able to access content through multiple modalities, whether it’s over-the-air broadcast, social media platforms, or free. If you were to look at Peacock, not only do we distribute NBC News, we distribute all of our own stations as well. I could be watching the Los Angeles local news in New York or I could be watching the Philadelphia local news. There’s no shortage of ways that we are supporting the public good in giving them multiple ways and choices in how they want to consume and access their news programming, and I don’t think that’s going to change. I think we’re going to continue to advocate for freedom of speech and freedom of the press. I think our news organization has been doing an unbelievable job in the product and the service that they’re doing for the public. Yeah. Matt, you can tell that’s an important topic for me for a lot of reasons. What’s next for NBCUniversal Media Group? What’s next for Peacock? What should people be looking for? I think what’s next for NBCUniversal Media Group is, as we talked about, we will likely be a separate company as part of the new NBC this time next year. You’ve got to come back. There’s a bunch of questions where I knew I wasn’t going to get answers because the deal isn’t closed yet. When that closes, you’ve got to come back because I have a million questions. I will definitely come back. I’m really looking forward to it. I think the other piece, as you know, is that we had our Q3 earnings last week. We talked a lot about Peacock and how we had a very different strategy with Peacock from the others when we launched our service six years ago. I’m really proud to share that Peacock was profitable in Q3 for the second consecutive quarter. We had $261 million of EBITDA. That’s $470 million better year-over-year. I think the team has done an unbelievable job, and I feel really good about our momentum and continuing to grow. It’s good proof that there’s not one way to go to market. There’s not one strategy or approach. You’ve got to play your hand and to your strengths, and you’re going to see us continue to do that at NBCUniversal. Yeah. We didn’t even talk about what AI might do to the cost structure of video. When you come back, we’re going to get into it. Matt, thank you so much for being on Decoder . Thank you so much. Questions or comments? Hit us up at decoder@theverge.com. We really do read every email!

articles.content: Sunday’s win at Liverpool showed the Gunners are deeper, more experienced, and are playing against a weaker class of contenders than last season Sign up for our free newsletter here Arsenal are three points clear at the top of the Premier League table . But given the team in second are Manchester City, who are likely to be facing at the very least a major points deduction , perhaps more significant is that they are five clear of Brighton in third. The season of domination that many anticipated from the champions appears to be coming to pass. Liverpool challenged them on Sunday. There was a 20-minute spell before half-time when they swarmed all over Arsenal, and Anfield felt at least like it did in the golden years of Jürgen Klopp, when it buzzed with an energy that could overwhelm visitors. But Arsenal got through that, reset at half-time, and navigated the second half with relative comfort. For the second league game running, they denied Liverpool a shot on target. articles.summary: I thought the explanation I’d given about black holes was family-friendly; but after what she had said, I had to rethink my examples Read more in the a job that changed me series In the first year of my science degree, I was fortunate to land a job as an…
articles.content: I thought the explanation I’d given about black holes was family-friendly; but after what she had said, I had to rethink my examples Read more in the a job that changed me series In the first year of my science degree, I was fortunate to land a job as an astronomy guide at the Sydney Observatory. In my role, I would lead tour groups of about 20 people. We’d look at stars and planets through telescopes. If the skies were filled from horizon to horizon with clouds, we’d explore more of the universe through a 3D theatre. And to peer beyond what our telescopes could see, we’d pile inside the cosy planetarium, seeing what the light pollution of Sydney and clouds would often obstruct from our view. My favourite object to show in the planetarium was the Hubble Ultra Deep Field image. Before revealing the image, I’d explain how the Hubble space telescope had stared at a piece of sky the size of a grain of sand held at arm’s length for 11 days, collecting enough light to look into the farthest corners of the universe. Then I’d zoom in on that tiny piece of sky, revealing the gorgeous image. At least one person would audibly gasp at the reveal. Continue reading...

articles.content: Many treatments are now extending lives, but the measure of progress should not end with a scan or a survival curve Two decades ago, a dear friend called me in a trembling voice. Was there hope for his young nephew , whose cancer had spread to the brain? Sadly, “no”, I said. But today, for such patients, there are options that were unimaginable back then. Recently, researchers at the European Society For Medical Oncology presented the latest chapter results from a randomised controlled trial of a bespoke cancer vaccine for patients with high-risk melanoma. The trial involved 1,137 patients whose melanoma had been surgically removed but remained at high recurrence risk. They received either pembrolizumab, an established immunotherapy, or pembrolizumab combined with an experimental mRNA vaccine, designed to help the immune system recognise and attack targets unique to the patient’s tumour. articles.content: Mercedes driver makes history at 20 years old by exceeding all expectations in only his second season Before the 2026 season had begun there was something of a consensus within Formula One. Mercedes appeared to have the fastest car and George Russell was favourite for the title. Beside him in what was indeed a dominant Mercedes, his teenage teammate, Kimi Antonelli, was the prodigious talent who was expected to require honing after a tricky rookie season. Said consensus lasted one race, by the sixth it had been turned on its head and Antonelli was squarely on his way to being champion. Few had doubted that the then 19-year-old Italian would prove to be strong in a car that for the first two-thirds of the season was the class of the field but for Antonelli to come out of the blocks with such verve, aggressive skill and also the judgment and at times maturity of a veteran was revelatory. As the youngest F1 world champion and Italy’s first since Alberto Ascari in 1953, Antonelli made history this year but it was the way he did it which truly caught the eye. Continue reading...

articles.title: Zero passing yards, one win. Did the Bucs just reinvent the NFL in all the wrong ways?
articles.summary: In a downpour against the Atlanta Falcons, Tampa Bay decided throwing was for losers. They were proved right I don’t think I’m being cheeky when I say that passing is the most exciting part of football. A solid hit is nice, and a big run can thrill you, but…
articles.content: In a downpour against the Atlanta Falcons, Tampa Bay decided throwing was for losers. They were proved right I don’t think I’m being cheeky when I say that passing is the most exciting part of football. A solid hit is nice, and a big run can thrill you, but this is a quarterback-centric game. When a QB is bad, teams usually lose and fans get bored. So, Sunday’s performance by Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers had me positively gobsmacked. I wouldn’t say their 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons was thrill-a-minute, but it certainly was historic. By completing a grand total of zero passes out of a paltry three attempts, Baker Mayfield led the Bucs to the first game with no passing offense since the Buffalo Bills beat the New York Jets 16-12 on 29 September 1974. If you are miraculously old enough to remember the NFL before the advent of the forward pass in 1906, first off, congratulations on being over 120 years of age. Please email me your full diet and exercise regimen. You’re probably on your feet (if standing is still something physically possible), cheering a bit of hard-nosed, classic football. The rest of us young whippersnappers still grinding through our first century are holding our noses. Of course, Mayfield – a former No 1 overall pick – can throw. As recently as 2024 he threw for 41 touchdowns and 4,500 passing yards in a season. But Sunday’s game was played in pouring rain that led to farcical moments like this , and Tampa Bay clearly decided that the ground game was the only way to go. That the Bucs could score at all, let alone 16 points, is a credit to Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell running as though their lives depended on it. Irving finished the day with 170 rushing yards and one touchdown, while Gainwell had 140. Combined with Mayfield, they rushed 56 times for 324 yards – the most ever in a single game for the Bucs. They more than made up for Mayfield’s borderline irrelevance in the pocket. Mayfield made himself useful blocking for his runners, but otherwise, I probably could have started at QB for the Buccaneers and the game would have been the same, other than the high likelihood of me suffering at least one gruesome injury. Continue reading...

articles.aiArticle:
After **35 years** of operations, the United Nations peacekeeping mission dedicated to the disputed territory of Western Sahara officially ceased its activities on **Sunday**, according to NPR Topics: World. 

## Decades of Conflict Over Former Spanish Territory
The territory in question was previously under Spanish rule before becoming the center of a long-standing sovereignty dispute, the report states. Control of the region is contested by **Morocco** and the pro-independence **Polisario Front**, leaving international diplomats to manage a fragile status quo for decades. The closure of the mission marks the end of a protracted chapter in international peacekeeping efforts across North Africa, wrapping up more than three decades of continuous monitoring and diplomatic engagement by the global body.

International conflicts and regional territorial disputes often leave lasting impacts on civilian populations, forcing many to navigate years of uncertainty or displacement, similar to how communities face prolonged hardships in other conflict zones, such as when families endure ['We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied front-line city](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/we-came-back-from-hell-say-ukrainians-after-years-in-russia-occupied).

*Context:* The termination of this longstanding U.N. mandate alters the diplomatic framework surrounding Western Sahara, potentially shifting regional power dynamics between Morocco and the Polisario Front. Without an active international peacekeeping presence on the ground, the risk of renewed tension or escalation increases, directly affecting Sahrawi civilians and regional stability. Observers note that the withdrawal forces local and international actors to reconsider how future self-determination efforts or negotiations might be pursued without direct U.N. oversight.

## What to Watch

Hungary’s incoming administration is set to publish the identities of **tens of thousands** of state informants who collaborated with security police during the communist era, according to World news | The Guardian. Scheduled for **Wednesday**, the mass unmasking targets records compiled between **1945 and 1989**, a period when the regime utilized a vast network of spies to crush political dissent. The upcoming transparency push aims to restore fractured public trust by lifting the veil on decades of historical secrecy.

## Uncovering Decades of State Surveillance

During the four decades of communist rule, security forces depended heavily on ordinary citizens turning on neighbors, colleagues, and family members. According to the report, the newly elected government insists that exposing these collaborators is a necessary step to address historical grievances and heal national divisions. For generations, suspicions have lingered over who cooperated with the regime, creating an environment where rumors often poisoned interpersonal relationships long after the political system collapsed. 

Historical reckonings with secret police archives have followed varied paths across Eastern Europe since the fall of the Iron Curtain, often stirring intense public debate over collective guilt versus individual accountability. Similar transitions in the region, as detailed in our analysis on [how the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/how-the-downfall-of-serbia-s-vučiċ-mirrored-that-of-hungary-s), show how past authoritarian legacies continue to shape modern political struggles.

## Why This Matters

Context: Opening these archives strikes at the core of national memory, forcing contemporary society to confront uncomfortable truths about complicity under totalitarian rule. For many families, the disclosures risk shattering long-held illusions about relatives or acquaintances, transforming abstract historical oppression into immediate, personal betrayal. Critics and supporters alike recognize that while transparency can offer closure, it also threatens to open old wounds in a country where political divisions remain sharp.

## What to Watch

Context: Observers will be monitoring the immediate public reaction following Wednesday's document release, specifically how civil society groups and legal experts respond to potential privacy disputes or contested file accuracy.

articles.aiArticle:
A coalition of **360 sports figures** has thrown its weight behind an appeal to the prime minister, urging the government to expand financial support for Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME) research. According to **BBC Sport**, the prominent athletic community members put their names to an open letter demanding direct action and a meeting with **Beth Dobbin**. 

The coordinated public appeal seeks to draw high-level political attention to a chronic condition that has historically suffered from underfunding. By leveraging their collective platform, the signatories aim to push Whitehall into shifting its resource allocation toward biomedical studies into the debilitating illness. 

## The Broader Context of Medical Advocacy

articles.title: Alex Garland’s Elden Ring adaptation is on course to be Hollywood’s goriest ever fantasy movie
articles.summary: The expansive project has hype and money behind it – but how do you avoid it falling into the disappointment trap so many films end up stumbling into? If the history of failed Hollywood fantasy projects over the past 20 years has taught us anything, it is…
articles.content: The expansive project has hype and money behind it – but how do you avoid it falling into the disappointment trap so many films end up stumbling into? If the history of failed Hollywood fantasy projects over the past 20 years has taught us anything, it is that transporting audiences to another world is only half the battle: you also have to give them a reason to spend several hours there. The Golden Compass diluted Philip Pullman’s theological bite, Warcraft thought that just explaining its world would make us care about it, and The Dark Tower compressed Stephen King’s sprawling mythology so ruthlessly that it scarcely left room for a story. All these films at one point had fans of the original source material quivering with anticipation at the prospect of seeing their beloved worlds on the big screen; all ended up disappointing. Which brings us to the forthcoming Alex Garland adaptation of the hugely popular high fantasy video game, Elden Ring. If there was ever a cinematic test of the phrase “too big to fail”, it is surely this. Elden Ring has sold more than 30m copies and is widely regarded as one of the greatest video games ever made. George RR Martin himself wrote the foundational mythology of warring demigods that underpins its gorgeous fantasy hellscape. And Garland as writer-director seems almost impossibly perfect: as the creative behind Dredd, Ex Machina and Annihilation, he has both the taste for beautiful nightmares and the geek credentials to deliver something extraordinary. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘They said we incited riots’: explosive punks Bad Brains on drugs, self-destruction and recording from jail
articles.summary: Young, black and fuelled by self-help mantras, they were reputedly the best live band on Earth. As their wild first sessions are rereleased, the group talk about scaring club owners – and getting kicked out of the UK Old punks might not agree on much – who…
articles.content: Young, black and fuelled by self-help mantras, they were reputedly the best live band on Earth. As their wild first sessions are rereleased, the group talk about scaring club owners – and getting kicked out of the UK Old punks might not agree on much – who was first, who was fastest, where to file the Faith/Void split LP in their record collection – but for those who saw them in their prime, Bad Brains were, unequivocally, the best live band on the planet. YouTube footage bears this out: frontman HR, born Paul D Hudson, is equal parts straining sinew and raw electricity as he bucks and contorts, punctuating rapid-fire snarls and otherworldly croons with impeccably timed backflips. The band surge around him, forging blisteringly fast punk informed by everything from the Damned and Dead Boys to P-Funk, Stevie Wonder and Chick Corea’s Return to Forever. Young, black and fuelled by an ideology that united the 1930s self-help mantras of Napoleon Hill with Rastafari, they were outliers in the already outre 70s punk scene. But while Bad Brains helped change the face of American punk as it morphed into hardcore in the early 80s, and inspired artists as diverse as Rage Against the Machine, Deftones, Lil Jon, the Roots and Beastie Boys, defeat was never far from glory as they balanced feted live performances and a scintillating run of records with an excruciating capacity for self-sabotage. Cryptocurrency exchanges function as digital marketplaces where users buy, sell, and store various virtual currencies, often holding vast pools of customer liquidity. articles.title: Democrats have high hopes for midterms, but polls have let them down before
articles.summary: Polls have been predicting a Democratic surge, but last-minute deciders and sampling issues mean there's no guarantee.
articles.content: Polls have been predicting a Democratic surge, but last-minute deciders and sampling issues mean there's no guarantee.
articles.aiArticle:
As the political map shifts in the final hours before the vote, the Democratic Party is once again confronting the familiar and uneasy sensation of high expectations colliding with survey data. According to **BBC News**, public opinion surveys currently point toward a robust Democratic surge, yet party strategists and veteran observers remain intensely cautious about what the final ballots will actually reveal. 

Midterm elections in the United States have historically carried enormous consequences for the sitting administration, frequently reshaping the legislative power balance in Washington and influencing everything from domestic spending to international policy. For voters across the country, these contests determine which party controls the levers of Congress, affecting communities from major urban centers to rural districts where economic anxiety runs high. Readers often look at these dynamics through various regional lenses, much like how voters evaluate [Democrats running in difficult states like Texas](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/democrats-are-used-to-heartbreak-in-texas-could-talarico-turn-the-tide) where shifting demographics create complex political challenges.

## Polling Vulnerabilities and Undecided Voters

The reliability of pre-election surveys has faced intense scrutiny in recent cycles, and the current contest is no exception. The report states that last-minute deciders—those citizens who walk into the voting booth without having made up their minds days prior—possess the capacity to completely disrupt statistical projections. Furthermore, pollsters continue to grapple with persistent sampling issues that make it difficult to capture an accurate cross-section of the electorate. 

While public surveys provide a useful snapshot of political momentum, history shows they can harbor significant blind spots when turnout models fail. Past cycles have demonstrated that enthusiasm gaps and sudden shifts among independent voters can render final polling averages misleading. This inherent volatility explains why campaign managers on both sides treat numbers with a heavy dose of skepticism until the actual count begins.

## Understanding the Stakes

Analysts note that midterm cycles serve as an essential referendum on the current political establishment, carrying profound implications for legislative agendas and executive power. When polling numbers diverge from reality, the fallout can alter the direction of national policy for years, impacting millions of citizens who rely on federal programs, economic stability, and legislative reform. 

Political analysts will be monitoring how polling methodologies hold up against actual voter turnout, particularly regarding late-breaking decisions in competitive districts. Observers will also track how parties manage voter mobilization efforts in the final stretch, as ground games frequently overcome the statistical advantages suggested by public surveys.

Sources: [BBC News](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmg47p3edv4do?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

When civil demonstrations descend into lethal attacks utilizing petrol bombs, the state response invariably hardens, risking a cycle of escalating violence and diminished civil liberties. For local businesses, commuters, and residents in affected urban areas, the recurring weekend chaos disrupts daily life and inflicts property damage. articles.summary: The Covid pandemic shed an unforgiving light on health and social care inequalities. The lessons have yet to be absorbed The fear that so many felt as the death toll rose during the Covid pandemic was magnified for Fiona Walker. “I know from experience they…
articles.content: The Covid pandemic shed an unforgiving light on health and social care inequalities. The lessons have yet to be absorbed The fear that so many felt as the death toll rose during the Covid pandemic was magnified for Fiona Walker. “I know from experience they wouldn’t have valued my life,” she says, in a new report on the treatment of people with learning disabilities during the crisis. The 1.5 million people in the UK with learning disabilities, and their families, had reason for concern. Death rates in England were four to six times higher than average for people with learning disabilities. As is now well established, the pandemic did not create inequalities; it exposed and intensified them. People with learning disabilities die on average 19.5 years earlier than people without, and deaths are almost twice as likely to be classed as avoidable. Continue reading...

A fresh series of military strikes conducted by Israel across the Gaza Strip has resulted in the deaths of **eight** people, according to local medical officials and reporting by BBC News. The latest casualties include **five** members of the Hamas-administered police force alongside **three** civilians in a separate incident, heightening tensions in an already volatile region. 

## Casualties Reported in Khan Younis and Gaza City

According to the BBC News report, the violence unfolded across multiple urban centers within the Palestinian territory. In the southern city of **Khan Younis**, an Israeli attack targeted and killed **five** officers belonging to the Hamas-run police department. Meanwhile, a distinct strike in **Gaza City** claimed the lives of **three** individuals, which local health officials confirmed included at least **one child**. Medical personnel at area hospitals processed the casualties as rescue teams responded to the sites of the impacts. 

The ongoing military operations are part of a broader, protracted conflict that has devastated civilian infrastructure and displaced millions of residents across the enclave since hostilities escalated significantly. Humanitarian agencies operating in the area have repeatedly warned about the severe risks posed to non-combatants trapped in densely populated urban zones during active military engagements.

## Analyzing the Humanitarian Impact

The stakes in this ongoing escalation extend far beyond the immediate casualty figures, deeply affecting millions of civilians who face chronic shortages of medical care, clean water, and shelter. As hospitals struggle to cope with an influx of wounded patients amid dwindling supplies, the humanitarian situation continues to deteriorate rapidly.
